notes: Parses via libcurl's URL API (`curl_url`/`curl_url_set`/`curl_url_get`) rather than a hand-rolled parser — the same "reuse the already-linked C library" approach `fetch` established

`new URL(url, base)` resolves a relative `url` against `base` ([ADR-00579](../adr/ADR-00579.md)) — curl's own relative resolution: an absolute `url` overwrites `base`, and an invalid `base` throws ("Invalid URL"), matching Node

Component **setters** (`url.hash = …`, `url.protocol = …`, etc.) re-parse the URL and re-derive every field so the components never desync ([ADR-00572](../adr/ADR-00572.md)): marker normalization matches Node (`#`/`?` on hash/search, a trailing `:` on protocol are tolerated); an invalid `href` assignment throws, the other setters silently ignore an invalid value (Node's own behavior); `searchParams` re-populates from the new query

Setters cover `href`/`protocol`/`host`/`hostname`/`port`/`pathname`/`search`/`hash`/`username`/`password` ([ADR-00577](../adr/ADR-00577.md)); `host` splits on the first `:` into hostname + port, and a value with no port keeps the existing port (Node's own behavior)

Fields: `href`, `protocol`, `host`, `hostname`, `port`, `pathname`, `search`, `hash`, `origin`, `username`, `password`, `searchParams` — all plain reads via the ordinary object field-access path, no dispatched methods

WHATWG normalization ([ADR-00874](../adr/ADR-00874.md)/[TDD-00203](../tdd/TDD-00203.md)): a default port is stripped (`new URL('http://example.com:80/x').port` is `''`) and the host is lowercased (`new URL('HTTP://ExAmple.COM/x').hostname` is `'example.com'`)

The WHATWG **static** methods `URL.parse(input[, base])` → `URL \| null` and `URL.canParse(input[, base])` → `boolean` are implemented (non-throwing, unlike `new URL()`) — distinct from the legacy lowercase `url.parse()` module function below
`JSON.stringify(url)` honors `URL.prototype.toJSON()` (returns `href`), so it serializes the `href` string, not the component struct
A part absent from the URL (no port/query/fragment) reads as `""`, matching real `URL`'s own default
Throws a catchable Error ("Invalid URL") on a malformed URL

`URL`/`URLSearchParams` are ambient globals — no import needed, and identical in browsers and Node (Node also re-exports them from `node:url`); the legacy `url.*` helpers below are Node-only and require `import … from 'node:url'`
See [ADR-00076](../adr/ADR-00076.md)
caveats: A non-ASCII hostname is case-folded and punycoded, without the rest of UTS 46's mapping: a full-width `ＥＸＡＭＰＬＥ.com` punycodes where Node reads `example.com`
Spreading a `URLSearchParams` directly (`[...params]`) yields an empty array — the same pre-existing limitation as `[...map]`; use `[...params.entries()]` (which works). Not URLSearchParams-specific.
notes: `url.searchParams` is **live**: `append`/`set`/`delete`/`sort` on it re-serialize the query back into `url.search`/`url.href` ([ADR-00966](../adr/ADR-00966.md)); the handle keeps its identity across a mutation, and emptying the query drops `search` to `""`. A standalone `new URLSearchParams(...)` has no owning URL and is unaffected

Backed by an ordered name/value **pair list** (the WHATWG "list of tuples", [ADR-00873](../adr/ADR-00873.md)/[TDD-00203](../tdd/TDD-00203.md)) — replaces the former `Map<string,string>`, so duplicate keys and cross-key insertion order round-trip faithfully (`?a=1&b=2&a=3` → `getAll('a')` is `['1','3']`)

Full method surface: `append`/`set` (replace-first-drop-rest)/`get` (first match, `null` if absent)/`getAll`/`has`/`delete`/`sort` (stable, by key)/`size`, plus `keys()`/`values()`/`entries()`/`forEach()`, `for…of` iteration (default iterator = entries), and `console.log` rendering — `has`/`delete` accept the WHATWG optional 2nd `value` argument

`toString()` serializes application/x-www-form-urlencoded (a space is `+`, not `%20`); a non-string name/value is stringified (`append('n', 1)` → `"1"`); `params + ''` / `` `${params}` `` serialize via `toString`
`new URLSearchParams(init)`: a query string (leading `?` tolerated), an array of `[name, value]` pairs, a record object, or another `URLSearchParams` (copied)
See [ADR-00076](../adr/ADR-00076.md)

caveats: Object-literal init only, over `protocol`/`hostname`/`port`/`pathname`/`search`/`hash`/`username`/`password` ([ADR-00585](../adr/ADR-00585.md)) — no constructor-string form, no `baseURL`
Pattern grammar is literals, `\` escapes, `*`, `:name`, and `:name?` — `{}` groups, `+` modifiers, and inline `(regex)` groups throw a `TypeError` at construction

`.exec()` returns a merged `Map<string, string> \| null` of every named group across components (an unset optional group is absent), not the spec's per-component `URLPatternResult` object — needs the dynamic object model ([TDD-00155](../tdd/TDD-00155.md))
`*` wildcards aren't exposed as numbered groups; no `hasRegExpGroups`
notes: Each component pattern compiles once at construction to an anchored PCRE2 regex (embedded C runtime); input URLs parse via libcurl's URL API, so `.test`/`.exec` link `-lpcre2-8` + `-lcurl` — both already conditional. An unparseable input is `false`/`null`, never a throw; an omitted init component defaults to `*` and reads back as such from the component fields ([TDD-00100](../tdd/TDD-00100.md)/[ADR-00311](../adr/ADR-00311.md))

caveats: The `parseQueryString` object form of `query` is a dictionary held in a union field: reading it after narrowing works, but `console.log`/`JSON.stringify` of it through `any` do not see its keys ([ADR-01225](../adr/ADR-01225.md))
notes: Node's own lib/url.js, in TypeScript (`lib/node/internal_url.ts`): the lenient never-throw parse, `null` for an absent component, `slashes`, backslash handling, auto-escaping, and the DEP0169 warning once per process ([ADR-01221](../adr/ADR-01221.md))
Importable named (`import { parse } from 'url'`), via namespace, and via default; `Url` and its `parse`/`format`/`resolve`/`resolveObject` methods are exported too

lib/url.js's `urlFormat`: a `Url`-shaped object (slashed protocols, `[ipv6]` hosts, `query` objects through `querystring.stringify`, `#`/`?` escaping in the pathname), a string (parsed then formatted), or a WHATWG `URL` with the `auth`/`fragment`/`search`/`unicode` options ([ADR-01221](../adr/ADR-01221.md))

Converts a `file:` URL (string or WHATWG `URL`) to the percent-decoded filesystem path; throws on a non-`file:` scheme. On Windows `file:///C:/dir/f` is `C:\dir\f` and `file://server/share/f` is the UNC path `\\server\share\f` ([ADR-00722](../adr/ADR-00722.md))

`{ windows }` picks the flavor on any host — a literal at compile time, a run-time boolean through both halves — and `undefined` means the host; the POSIX half throws Node's `File URL host must be "localhost" or empty on <platform>` for a non-empty, non-`localhost` host and rejects an encoded `/`; neither half goes through libcurl, which refuses a drive letter in a file URL on Linux/macOS ([ADR-01079](../adr/ADR-01079.md))
`{ windows }` selects the win32 (`file:///C:/dir/f`, UNC host) or POSIX form on any host, `undefined` meaning the host's ([ADR-01079](../adr/ADR-01079.md))

Resolves the path to absolute, percent-encodes it, and returns a WHATWG `URL` with the `file:` scheme; on Windows a drive path is `file:///C:/dir/f` and a UNC path keeps its server as the host ([ADR-00722](../adr/ADR-00722.md))

The escape set is Node's, not libcurl's: controls, space, `" # % < > ? [ ] ^ { | } ~`, the backtick and every non-ASCII byte become upper-case `%XX`; the sub-delims `! $ & ' ( ) * + , ; = @` stay literal; `href` and `pathname` agree ([ADR-01046](../adr/ADR-01046.md))

lib/url.js's `urlResolve`/`resolveObject`: relative paths, `..`/`.` segments, protocol-relative and cross-protocol targets, non-slashed schemes (`mailto:`), with `url.resolveObject` alongside ([ADR-01221](../adr/ADR-01221.md))

caveats: Expects a WHATWG `URL`; a legacy `Url`/plain object isn't accepted ([ADR-00672](../adr/ADR-00672.md))
notes: Remaps a `URL` into the `http.request` option bag (`protocol`/`hostname`/`hash`/`search`/`pathname`/`path`/`href`/`port`/`auth`)

caveats: IDN conversion of a **non-ASCII** domain requires the libcurl build to include an IDN backend (libidn2) — present on typical Linux, **absent on the Mac build** where a non-ASCII domain returns `""` (Node's own failure contract). ASCII domains pass through everywhere ([ADR-00672](../adr/ADR-00672.md))
notes: Punycode/IDN conversion via libcurl (`CURLU_PUNYCODE`/`CURLU_PUNY2IDN`), ASCII letters lowercased as the WHATWG host parser does; returns `""` on failure, matching Node ([ADR-01221](../adr/ADR-01221.md))
